title: GPU Pool Assistant & Scaling Workbench — interactive health, tuning and burst controls
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and prototype an integrated "GPU Pool Assistant & Scaling Workbench" for Redwood Console dedicated capacity dashboards. The scope covers a single-pane UI that combines real-time pool health, proactive tuning suggestions, interactive autoscale rule editing, burst controls, and a cost/latency preview. Deliverables: Figma prototype, annotated handoff, accessibility checklist, and a short usability session summary. Goal: reduce on-call hunting and provide SRE/Platform teams with an opinionated, reversible set of controls for predictable capacity and graceful bursts.
comments: 2026-02-11 — Maya Chen: Kickoff with PM and Eng. Framing: reduce mean-time-to-resolution for pool incidents and simplify burst ops. Agreed success metrics: 30% faster incident triage (measured via playbook runs), 15% fewer manual scale-ups for predictable workloads.

2026-02-17 — Design exploration v0 complete (link to Figma file: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/gpu-pool-workbench). Two top-level concepts: (A) Compact 'health + actions' header for quick ops (B) Expanded 'workbench' mode with timeline replay, predictive recommendations, and sandboxed rule simulation.

2026-02-21 — Engineering feedback (Diego): prefer server side for rule validation; we can submit a dry-run API to evaluate autoscale changes. Need to keep the UI lightweight to avoid extra telemetry queries at load. Agreed to lazy-load the timeline and heavy metrics.

2026-02-25 — PM review (Arjun Patel): prioritize cost-preview when editing burst size; business asks for explicit 'estimated monthly delta' before save. Added a small cost model we can compute client-side with rate-limited tokens from the cost endpoint.

2026-03-02 — Usability testing (5 internal participants). Findings: users liked the 'What will change' diff panel when modifying rules. Confusion around 'min_replicas' vs 'stable_capacity' naming — updated copy to 'Base capacity (min)' and 'Target concurrency'.

2026-03-05 — Design iteration v1 uploaded. New components: Health Rings (per-GPU temp/queued-requests/warm-cache %), Autoscale Rule Composer (drag-and-drop triggers), Burst Simulator (time window slider + estimated token cost). Prototype link: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/gpu-pool-workbench-v1

2026-03-07 — Accessibility pass: color contrast adjusted for status badges, keyboard support added for the timeline scrubber, screen reader labels added to the autoscale rule tokens. Documented checklist in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/infra/GPU+Pool+Assistant+Accessibility

2026-03-09 — Design review notes from Eng (Lena Kovács): please add a fallback card that surfaces compatible model variants when the pool is at 95% capacity; backend can expose 'compatible_models' in the health API. Also recommend a compact mode for dashboards with many pools (table row quick-actions).

2026-03-10 — PM final review (Arjun Patel): Approved for engineering grooming. Add 'rollback to previous rule' CTA after any rule change and include audit log link in the confirmation modal. Request that the cost delta is persisted to usage analytics for billing signals.

Design follow-ups: polish mobile/tablet compact mode, finalize microcopy for audit flows. TAG: design-ready-for-grooming.
